title: Attractor
summary: An attractor is an invariant set approached by trajectories from a nontrivial basin, under a specified definition.

context.note: Revision 2 exposes a QEVA foundation dependency instead of stopping only at a textual framework label.

assumptions.text: A dynamical system, invariant set A, metric, and basin notion are specified.

content.plain: An attractor is long-run structure toward which many permitted starting states move.
content.exact: One common definition: a compact invariant set A is an attractor if there exists a neighborhood U of A such that dist(F^n(x),A)→0 for every x∈U, often with an additional minimality condition.
content.example: For F(x)=x/2 on R, {0} is an attractor for all initial x.
content.caveat: Attractor definitions vary across dynamical-systems literature; “strange attractor” additionally needs explicitly stated properties.

relations.note: Attracting behavior is analyzed together with stability.
A stable fixed point may be an attractor.
